Read a hydrometric series from a CSV file

Source: R/prepare.R
read_hydro_series.Rd

Reads one series of rain, evaporation or flow from the layouts hydrometric exports use:

Usage

read_hydro_series(
  file,
  value_col = NULL,
  time_col = NULL,
  time_formats = .time_formats,
  tz = "UTC",
  na_strings = c("", "NA", "NaN", "-", "---", "-9999")
)

Arguments

file

Path of the CSV file.

value_col

Name of the value column; by default the last numeric column.

time_col

Name of the time column, or of a date and a time column; by default found.

time_formats

Formats to try, in order; the first that reads 99% of the times is used.

tz

Time zone of the times in the file. EA telemetry is in GMT all year: "UTC".

na_strings

Strings read as missing.

Value

A pdm_hydro_series: a data frame of time (POSIXct, UTC) and value, with the file, the columns used and the median step in minutes as attribute source.

Details

  • Split date columns: year, month and day columns, with hour, minute and second if present, in any of their usual spellings (hour or hours, min or minute).

  • One time column, or a date column and a time column side by side, in any of the common formats (2021-03-01 09:15, 01/03/2021 09:15, ISO 8601 and others).

The value is the last numeric column unless named. Times are read in tz and returned in UTC. Rows whose time cannot be read are dropped, and a file whose timestamps repeat is refused: repeats mean a time column was missed, and keeping one value per time would calibrate on a fraction of the record.

See also

align_series(), check_inputs()

Examples

f <- tempfile(fileext = ".csv")
writeLines(c("year,month,day,hour,minute,flow", "2021,3,1,9,0,1.2", "2021,3,1,9,15,1.3"), f)
read_hydro_series(f)
#> Hydrometric series from file1001426547c.csv: 2 rows, 2021-03-01 09:00 to 2021-03-01 09:15, step 15 min, 0 missing
#> Columns used: time year + month + day + hour + minute, value flow
